name: NVIDIA A100 SXM4 80GB (GA100, compute capability 8.0)
notes: Published figures, not a measurement: no device run has confirmed any of them, and none has run here. launch_ns, link_ns, memory_efficiency, occupancy_to_saturate and memory_latency_ns are assumptions, the same on every packaged card, marked as such below.

documents.datasheet: NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU datasheet, the A100 80GB SXM column (https://www.nvidia.com/content/dam/en-zz/Solutions/Data-Center/a100/pdf/nvidia-a100-datasheet-us-nvidia-1758950-r4-web.pdf)
documents.whitepaper: NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture whitepaper, Table 3 (https://images.nvidia.com/aem-dam/en-zz/Solutions/data-center/nvidia-ampere-architecture-whitepaper.pdf)
documents.hopper_whitepaper: NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture whitepaper, Table 3, the A100 column (https://resources.nvidia.com/en-us-hopper-architecture/nvidia-h100-tensor-c)
documents.guide: CUDA Programming Guide 13.4.2, Compute Capabilities, Tables 30 and 31 (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html)

source.sms: Ampere whitepaper: 108 SMs of 64 FP32 cores each, 6912 in all, GPU boost clock 1410 MHz; the 80GB SXM4's datasheet figures are the same compute at the same clock.
source.dram_gbps: Datasheet, A100 80GB SXM: GPU memory bandwidth 2,039 GB/s (HBM2e).
source.flops: Datasheet and Ampere whitepaper: FP32 19.5 TFLOPS (6912 cores, 2 operations per fused multiply-add, 1.41 GHz), FP64 9.7 TFLOPS. i32 is the Hopper whitepaper's Peak INT32 TOPS for A100, 19.5: 64 INT32 cores an SM, counted as the whitepapers count them, 2 operations per core a clock, the convention every packaged card follows.
source.tensor: Datasheet, dense (the sparse figures are twice these): TF32 Tensor Core 156 TFLOPS, BFLOAT16 and FP16 Tensor Core 312 TFLOPS. Compute capability 8.0 has no FP8 or FP4 tensor cores (Guide, Table 33). The model reads tensor_f16; the others are recorded for a reader.
source.link_gbps: Datasheet: PCIe Gen4 64 GB/s, both directions together, so 32 GB/s each way, before protocol overhead. NVLink joins GPUs to each other, not to the host.
source.occupancy: CUDA Programming Guide 13.4.2, Compute Capabilities, Tables 30 and 31 (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html), 8.0 column: 64 K registers, 64 warps (2048 threads) and 164 KB of shared memory an SM; the CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9, section 20, says for each of 8.x, 9.0, 10.x and 12.0 that the 1 KB of shared memory not made available to a thread block is reserved for system use (shared_reserved); the CUDA Occupancy Calculator allocates registers a warp at a time in units of 256 (register_unit). No limit on resident blocks per SM is applied here.
source.shared_bytes_per_clock: CUDA C++ Programming Guide: shared memory has 32 banks, each 32 bits wide a clock cycle.
source.memory_latency_ns: Assumed. NVIDIA publishes no device-memory latency and no run here has measured one; it prices only a pipeline's asynchronous copies, as the bytes in flight over this latency. Every packaged card assumes the same 500 ns.
